Definition: Bosmath, the name of a wife of Esau, and of a daughter of Solomon
BiblicalUsage: Bashemath means spice, and the name belongs to two women who must not be mixed up. In Genesis 26:34 Esau takes Bashemath the daughter of Elon the Hittite to wife, and in Genesis 36:3 and Genesis 36:4 another Bashemath, the daughter of Ishmael, bears Reuel to Esau. Then 1 Kings 4:15 names a different Basmath, the daughter of Solomon, who married Ahimaaz, one of his officers.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the two Bashemaths are a warning to read slowly: two wives of Esau with one name, and a daughter of Solomon with the same name again.
